text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created (pid=54822) 1 trace-export failures to Honeycomb detected. Auto-paging primary oncall.

oncall-bot: Paging sara (primary SRE) per policy: SRE-Pager -> Platform Escalation.

sara: getting repeated export errors from otel-collector: 'http response 503' and 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed'. Observability gap for distributed traces starting ~15:02 UTC.

matt: on my way. Is ingestion throttling global or region-specific?

jess: logs from collector: 
```
2026-03-15T15:05:12Z exporter/otlp.go:198 export failed: Post "https://api.honeycomb.io/v1/traces": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

leo: buffer queues in collector pod spiking, retry loops hitting max_retries and dropping spans. Drop rate jumped from 0.3% to 18% within 3 mins.

sara: toggling mitigation runbook step 1: switch to local persistent buffer + suspend immediate flush. Applying config to deployments.

jess: command to patch deployment env: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/otel-collector OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://local-sink.internal && \
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/otel-collector OTEL_EXPORTER_PERSISTENT_BUFFER=true
```

matt: applied to canary collectors. canary logs show local buffer writer writing to /var/otel/buffer and no outbound 503s.

inc-bot: Automated action recorded: env-change by matt. Runbook checkpoint: persistent-buffer ON.

ops-manager: quick note: CS reported one Dedicated customer who uses traces for billing correlate. Tag them and coordinate.

cs-tilly: sending heads-up now: "We're seeing trace export interruptions to Honeycomb; traces are being buffered and will be replayed once ingestion resumes. No application downtime."

leo: propose short-term sampling to reduce volume. I'll roll out lower sampling rate for high-volume namespaces.

sara: do it for non-Dedicated namespaces only. We cannot change sampling for customers with contractual observability SLAs.

jess: prepared patch for ConfigMap 'otel-sampling' with rate 0.4 for candidate namespaces. Command: 
```
kubectl -n services patch cm otel-sampling -p '{"data":{"global_rate":"0.4"}}'
```

matt: also set alert for local buffer > 75% to trigger scale-up or temporary disk allocation.

infra-bot: Alert: collector-buffer-usage (canary) = 68%. Watching.

leo: vendor status: https://status.honeycomb.io shows "degraded" ingestion in our default region. Vendor message: "We are investigating increased TLS handshake failures with our ingest endpoints."

jess: opened vendor ticket HC-9977 with full exporter stack traces and sample trace IDs. Uploaded sample payloads. Vendor acknowledged.

ops-manager: risk: if buffer fills, collectors may OOM or start dropping high-priority spans. Have remediation plan: increase EBS for collector nodes or fail open to long-term object store sink.

sara: I'll enable S3 sink as failover now (runbook step 3). Command: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/otel-collector OTEL_S3_BUCKET=redwood-otel-buffer && \
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/otel-collector OTEL_EXPORTER_S3_ENABLED=true
```

matt: S3 sink enabled on canary. upload throughput looks healthy. No further exporter 5xx from canary.

inc-bot: Incident status updated: mitigating 1 buffering to S3 + sampling reduced. Severity: P2 (observability degraded).

kate: preparing handoff note for next on-call. Key items: HC-9977 ticket open, buffering to S3 enabled, sampling at 0.4 for non-Dedicated, monitor buffer usage and collector restarts. If S3 queue > 90% escalate to ops-manager for capacity increase.

cs-tilly: customer notification sent at 15:40 UTC to impacted accounts.

leo: alternative considered: route traffic to backup telemetry ingest (NewRelic) for internal telemetry only. Blocker: data residency + schema mismatch + contract. Not approved for customer data.

jess: we can consider sending scrubbed internal spans to backup vendor (no PII) as an engineering telemetry fallback. Need legal review before any customer data hops vendors.

matt: vendor updated ticket: "We are rolling a patch to ingress TLS termination; expected to reduce handshake errors in 30-45m." They asked for continued samples if errors persist.

ops-manager: decide retention/replay policy: if vendor resolves within 48h we will replay buffered spans and mark reingested traces as 'replay=true'. If >48h discuss cost/opt-out for customers. Coordinate with product + legal.

sara: I'm staying on incident and will hand off at 19:00 UTC to kate. Handoff checklist: buffer stable, HC-9977 open, sample export uploaded, watch collector OOMs.

kate: I'll take at 19:00. If buffer grows beyond 80% before then ping me.

inc-bot: Handoff scheduled at 19:00 UTC.

jess: note for replay: ensure replay job adds attribute replayed=true and timestamp_replay_start. Also preserve original trace ids if possible. We'll coordinate with CS so customers can filter replayed traces.

cs-tilly: updated CS template to include guidance on replay and expected latency once reingest completes.

sara: final update for now: mitigation applied (S3 buffering + sampling), vendor ticket HC-9977 ongoing, no app-level impact. Monitoring and CS loop active. Will update on any vendor ETA changes. :white_check_mark:
